Rounded to the **nearest integer**, the area of the parallelogram $ABCD$ is{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
The diagonal $\overset{―}{AC}$ divides the parallelogram into two congruent triangles. Therefore, the area of the parallelogram is twice the area of $△ACB$ (see the illustration below).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946476/assets/d6a654d3154ba8af8fc4f7654e62c6bacfede7017322aeed21a143e2634dcd14.png)

 Computing the area of $△ACB,$ we find
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ACB} & =\frac{1}{2}(4)(8)\operatorname{sin}⁡{120}^{∘} \\  & =16\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{120}^{∘} \\  & ≈13.856,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places. Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & =2{A}_{ACB} \\  & =2\cdot 13.856 \\  & =27.712.\end{aligned}
$$

So, to the **nearest integer**, the area of the parallelogram is $28.$
